### Cap the feature loop's memory with a systemd scope

change `wmmltomzspwx` · [log `891d58bb4741`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/891d58bb4741cfc4975a702efa0d4705b1cfde5a4d7ab4b4fc55958571e0e113.jsonl.gz)

The feature loop ran as part of init.scope, the cgroup WSL shells start in, so a memory-hungry proof could exhaust the machine and take the WSL instance down. feature-loop.sh now re-executes itself in feature-loop.scope with a 4 GB cap (FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX) and no swap. It sets OOMPolicy=continue because the default stops the entire scope on the first kill, which would take claude down with the proof. It refuses to start when less memory than the cap is available or when the scope is still active.

Verified by running the real script with a stub claude on PATH under a 100M cap: the memory hog was killed with status 137, the stub survived, and the loop exited 1 through its usual no-commit path. Also checked refusal for a cap above available memory, an invalid cap and a second concurrent loop, exit 130 on systemctl stop, and that the scope unloads afterwards. A real proof run under the cap was not tested. The separate lib/ work in progress is left out of this commit.

### Limit each JBMC run's memory and report a run that dies as no verdict

change `qwoxmxwmqvqq` · [log `de33e7a7e157`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/de33e7a7e157258506656f319c290cff8ca6793d5d3bd32017ce756f83c9451b.jsonl.gz)

One regression proof, ModifiedUtf8#encodeInto, reached 5.7 GB, and nothing stopped it short of the whole machine. Each JBMC run now starts under a 3 GiB address-space limit, set with JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_MEMORY_MB, where 0 turns it off. Its raised oom_score_adj makes the kernel kill JBMC before the agent that launched it. A run that runs out of memory or is killed by a signal now reports unverifiable even if it had already printed a passing line; before, a killed run was not flagged at all.

This does not explain the last WSL crash: that session logged no OOM kills, and the VM was showing clock jumps and CPU stalls before the heavy work. The encodeInto proof now stops after about 16 seconds with 'JBMC ran out of memory', so it has no verdict yet. The README warns against --no-refine-strings, which proved a variant that deliberately differs.

Verified by the agent that wrote it, against the full working copy: 71 tests passed including 3 new ones, clippy was clean, and the encodeInto proof stopped at the limit. The tests were not rerun for this commit, which was split from uncommitted feature work; cargo check --all-targets passed on the split tree. The crosscut and quorum proofs and the feature loop end to end have not run under the limit.

### Add regression proofs over arrays

change `rmrslsqnnwnt` · [log `f0a55adc344b`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/f0a55adc344bf687db361879b86365a807d25b0aa3b1118b7a30597a93f9629f.jsonl.gz)

jvmcontract equivalence now accepts methods with array parameters and results. The harness copies each array argument exactly as long, runs the previous version on the copies and the new one on the originals, and compares results, exceptions and what each version leaves in the arrays, element by element, with two NaN results counting as equal. The scope in --unchanged-unless may quantify over an array. A differing input is shrunk in the interpreter and reported with what each version left behind. Replay and shrinking moved out of property.rs into a shared witness module. New options are --max-array-length and --no-shrink.

Verified with javac and jbmc on the PATH: all 71 tests pass, including the regression test over arrays, and clippy is clean. Written by the unattended feature loop before the crash; committed separately after the memory limits.

### Count only VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL as a proof

change `rkokwqwynkql` · [log `5b85100099cc`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/5b85100099cc9215cea9a67fdac266195cac8777d42786abea7ec3389c463d52.jsonl.gz)

parse_output treated '** 0 of N failed' as verified, but a solver that runs out of memory leaves every property as ERROR, so nothing has failed and JBMC ends with VERIFICATION ERROR and exit 6. With --no-refine-strings added through a wrapper, jvmcontract printed a proof that an encoder returning k + 1 behaves as before, and exited 0. Only VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL now counts, and the memory check no longer depends on capitalisation. In default mode six memory limits gave no false proof, but only because that path also happens to print 'Out of memory'.

Verified: the k + 1 reproduction now reports 'cannot be verified' and exits 1. The Quorum, Crosscut and Mica verify.sh scripts all pass under the 3 GiB limit, with 45 checks and no missing verdicts. This commit took over the description of a concurrent session's commit, whose array work is in the previous commit.

### Mark the encodeInto regression proof as pending, with a way to run it

change `zuuzotpskotx` · [log `ef935616497a`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/ef935616497a48429e3bb556cea20c1fd64ef735684b6769c6e077e5bde093be.jsonl.gz)

The regression proof of a fast path in ModifiedUtf8#encodeInto can't finish at the default bounds on this machine, and its patches had been lost with /tmp. examples/apps/mica/pending now holds both patches, a script that runs either one, what was measured, what a bounded proof doesn't say, and how to pick it up on a larger machine. change `sxnxlxoumsxk` · [log `703d2a06f61f`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/703d2a06f61f1e5a0fa45d3b5f08e720d077da65540f78c8222abd3ce20d0e86.jsonl.gz)

### Name overloaded targets by parameter types, and accept -2147483648

change `omkkonymrmpq` · [log `079307709b57`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/079307709b5792435cd91cf29506691717ae3b62c55c743894dc107027c96092.jsonl.gz)

A target may now name an overload by its parameter types, 'pkg.Class#pow(int, int)', in Java's spelling, simple or qualified. verifier::select_method does this for derive, equivalence and prove, and a bare overloaded name is refused with the list of overloads. ### Add the /verify-bytecode Claude Code skill, as a plugin with a one-command installer

change `sypzolsvlzwm` · [log `ce7ed5a6e273`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/ce7ed5a6e273f4765971bab2633deeea41841ecc2e7205d924b292222a813f23.jsonl.gz)

plugins/jvmcontract/ is a Claude Code plugin whose skill, /verify-bytecode &lt;pull request>, fetches a GitHub pull request as its merge base and head (scripts/fetch-pr.sh), compiles one module of each with Maven or Gradle and prints its classes and dependency classpath (scripts/build.sh, with a configuration-cache-safe Gradle init script), and then has the agent pick a proof per changed method: a regression proof with jvmcontract equivalence for static methods over primitives and integral arrays, a confined-change proof with --unchanged-unless when the pull request declares a change, a property proof of the Javadoc's @throws, @return and @param claims with jvmcontract prove, a behavioural contract diff for finite-domain methods, and capability and API contract diffs for the module, always. SKILL.md is the procedure, reference.md the tool's commands, expression language, refusals and measured costs for the agent, and report-template.md the report's shape. The skill runs on model: opus (Opus 5.5) and is only invoked explicitly. install.sh installs the skill into ~/.claude/skills, builds jvmcontract with cargo install --git (installing Rust first if needed), and checks for a JDK, JBMC, gh, build tools and jq; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json at the repo root makes 'claude plugin install jvmcontract --marketplace pilifs/in-the-loop' the other one-command path. The plugin README gives the install, what it proves, and five libraries to try it on (Commons Numbers, Joda-Time, Commons Codec, jackson-core, Commons Lang); the repo README links it. The landing page for terminalvalue.net/verify-bytecode-skill/ is in the Terminal-Value repository, not here.

On a real pull request, apache/commons-numbers#223, the regression proof of pow(int, int) found the fix's input pow(k=-2, e=31) (before: ArithmeticException, after: -2147483648) in 185 s; the Javadoc property proved in 1.4 s; the MIN_VALUE property proved on head in 1.0 s and was refuted on base in 0.7 s; the confined-change proof did not finish in 300 s. The Maven build of the external project could not be run in this session (the permission classifier declined it), so the changed file was compiled with javac alone; build.sh's Gradle path was verified on examples/apps/boxoffice and its Maven path only by reading.

Verified: the new integration test an_overloaded_method_is_named_by_its_parameter_types and the expression unit tests pass; the whole suite passed except one JBMC test that failed under contention with a concurrent proof and passed alone; the Terminal-Value site builds with the new page.

## What changed
- **Memory cap:** the script restarts itself inside `feature-loop.scope`, capped at 4 GB with no swap. To change the cap, set `FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX=3G` or similar. `jbmc`, TLC and Gradle all inherit it.
- **Fix to the diagnosis command:** it needs `-p OOMPolicy=continue`. Under the default, one memory kill stopped the whole scope in my test, which would have taken Claude and the current turn down with `jbmc`. Now only the process that ran out of memory dies, and the session sees it fail.
- **Won't start if:**
  - less memory is available than the cap
  - `feature-loop.scope` is still active from another loop or a leftover Gradle daemon; the error message gives the command to clear it
  - `systemd-run` fails, so it never falls back to running uncapped

The README section on the loop now covers this.

- Only the memory hog was killed (status 137); the fake `claude` survived, and the loop exited through its usual no-commit path.
- A cap above available memory, an invalid cap and a second loop were all refused.

## The `--no-refine-strings` problem
**The flag wasn't really the problem; `jvmcontract` was misreading a failed run as a proof.** I reproduced it: with the flag, it printed `✓ behaves as before on every input` and exited 0 for a method that deliberately returns the wrong answer.
- **What happened:** JBMC's solver ran out of memory, so every check ended as `ERROR`. JBMC then printed `** 0 of 4 failed` and `VERIFICATION ERROR` (exit 6). We read "0 failed" as proved.
- **The flag itself:** I saw no wrong verdict when it finished; at bound 2 it correctly caught the bug. At bound 8 it never finished, even with 5 GiB, so it doesn't help here. At bound 2 it used more memory, not less (911 MB vs 560 MB).
- **Default mode:** no false proof at six memory limits, but only because that path also prints `Out of memory`. I reviewed that check earlier and missed that it was case-sensitive.
- **Second bug:** temp file names could collide, so one proof could read another proof's output. A flaky test exposed it. The CLI runs proofs one at a time, but parallel library use and our integration tests were exposed.

**Already fixed:**
